messages:
Harper Lee: Quick usability note from support: customers want exported datasets to be round-trippable (export -> manifest -> re-import) so mappings persist. Can we include a manifest alongside CSV/ZIP?
Jonah Kim: Totally. Proposal: ZIP contains `data.csv`, `vectors.npy` (optional) and `manifest.json` with keys: dataset_name, filters_hash, column_order, mapping_version, export_tool_version.
Asha Rao: UX question: should manifest be optional or always included for ZIP? I vote always for ZIP, optional for CSV-only exports.
Elliot Park: Backend: easy to always write manifest for ZIP. For CSV-only we can add `--include-manifest` toggle. Need to document manifest schema.
Harper Lee: Copy: modal helper text: "ZIP exports include a machine-readable manifest to support re-import and reproducibility." Keep it short.
Jonah Kim: Manifest sample we discussed: { "dataset": "help-center", "filters": "f1a2b3", "columns": ["preview_text","rerank_score","owner"], "rows": 1248 } — include sha256 of CSV for integrity.
Asha Rao: Accessibility: screen reader should announce "Export job queued. Manifest will be included" and announce when the download link is ready including filename. Use aria-live.
a11y-bot: Recommend: aria-live="polite" for status updates and announce the filename + size when ready. Ensure focus is moved to the download link on completion.
Elliot Park: UX tweak: allow users to toggle "Friendly filename" vs "Compact filename". Friendly: `help-center-preview-f1a2b3-20260214.zip`. Compact: `hc-abc123.zip`. Default Friendly.
Harper Lee: Also request: rounding policy for rerank_score in exports. Many customers want a 3-decimal default and an advanced option "Full precision" for debugging.
Jonah Kim: Agree. We'll add precision dropdown: 3 / 5 / full. For CSV use text formatting e.g., `0.874` or `0.87412`. Also include locale-safe delimiting note for commas vs semicolons.
Asha Rao: Good point: CSV delimiter should default to comma but have an option for semicolon and Excel-friendly exports for locales that use comma decimal separators. Add a helper link "CSV formatting help".
Elliot Park: Small performance note: when including vectors.npy, compute size estimate and show approximate download size before starting job. If >200MB, auto-select queued job flow.
Harper Lee: UX microcopy for modal CTA: Primary = "Start export". Secondary = "Save mapping". Subtle helper: "Include manifest for reproducible imports" with a tooltip explaining manifest contents.
Jonah Kim: Mapping presets: add a small dropdown "Mapping: (none)" with quick actions: Save current mapping, Apply saved mapping, Manage mappings. Saved mappings stored per workspace.
Asha Rao: Accessibility: mappings dropdown must be reachable by keyboard and announce current mapping. Pressing M should focus mapping list.
a11y-bot: Suggest aria-keyshortcuts="M" on the mapping button and ensure announcement "Mapping applied: support-summary" when changed.
Elliot Park: Export retention: show in notification panel where exports live for 7 days with link to download again. For ZIP include manifest and a link to re-import flow.
Harper Lee: Small UI: add a preview snippet inside modal showing the first 2 rows of CSV with applied precision and delimiter so users can sanity check before export.
Jonah Kim: Final acceptance criteria: manifest included for ZIP, precision control, delimiter option, mapping presets, aria-live announcements, queued job for large files, preview sample. I'll file DX-4477 and assign.
Asha Rao: I'll mock the modal with the manifest helper, precision dropdown, and sample preview. Will include copy variations for the tooltip.
a11y-bot: Created accessibility checklist for DX-4477: focus trap, initial focus on primary control, aria-live for status, announce filename+size, keyboard shortcuts for mapping.
Harper Lee: Thanks team — will attach prototype and manifest schema to the ticket by EOD.
